'''Darializa Avila Chevalier''' (born {{birth based on age as of date|32|2026|1|25|noage=1}}),<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Fahy |first=Claire |date=June 24, 2026 |title=Who Is Darializa Avila Chevalier? |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/23/nyregion/who-is-darializa-avila-chevalier.html |access-date=June 24, 2026 |work= The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> also known as '''DAC''',<ref>{{cite news |last1=Beeferman |first1=Jason |last2=Fernandez |first2=Madison |last3=Sommerfeldt |first3=Chris |date=June 25, 2026 |title=The Dems already had AOC. Now they have DAC. |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/25/the-dems-already-had-aoc-now-they-have-dac-00975210 |work=[[Politico]] |access-date=October 31, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Davis |first1=Maya |date=July 9, 2026 |title=Meet the Socialists on Their Way to Capitol Hill |url=https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/democratic-socialist-candidates-congress-2026-d868b354 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]}}</ref> is an American politician and community organizer who is the [[U.S. Representative|U.S. Representative-elect]] for [[New York's 13th congressional district]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/new-york-us-house-district-13-results |title=New York House District 13 General Election Results 2026 |website=[[NBC News]] |access-date=November 4, 2026}}</ref> She is member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and the [[Democratic Socialists of America]].

Born and raised in [[Florida]], Avila Chevalier moved to [[New York City]] in 2012 to study at [[Columbia College, Columbia University|Columbia College]], where she received a Bachelor of Arts in [[Middle Eastern studies]]. She is a doctoral candidate in [[sociology]] at the [[City University of New York]], studying the way black immigrants from Latin America are impacted by the [[U.S. criminal justice system|U.S. criminal system]] and [[deportation]].

==Early life and education==
Avila Chevalier was born and raised in [[Florida]] to working-class [[Dominican Americans|Dominican immigrant]] parents.<ref name="AmsterdamNews2025Long">{{Cite news |last=Long |first=Ariama C. |title=Another political upstart? Darializa Avila Chevalier challenges U.S. Rep. Adriano Espaillat |url=https://amsterdamnews.com/news/2025/12/11/darializa-avila-chevalier-challenges-us-rep-adriano-espaillat/ |access-date=February 7, 2026 |work=[[Amsterdam News]] |date=December 11, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.westsidespirit.com/news/behind-avila-chevalier-s-stunning-victory-over-espaillat-in-c-d-13-JA5983795 |title=Behind Avila Chevalier's Stunning Victory over Espaillat in C.D. 13 |last=Oreskes |first=Michael |work=The Spirit |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 18, 2026}}</ref> Her father is a truck driver and her mother a [[caseworker]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hurwitz |first=Sophie |date=June 30, 2026 |title=Gaza is costing Democratic incumbents their seats |url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2026/06/encampments-democratic-party-chris-rabb-melat-kiros-darializa-chevalier/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=Mother Jones |language=en-US}}</ref> She also lived in the [[Dominican Republic]] and [[Venezuela]]<ref name="DiarioLasAmericas2026">{{Cite web |date=May 29, 2026 |title= Mamdani respalda a candidata socialista al Congreso, rival del veterano representante Adriano Espaillat |trans-title= Mamdani backs Socialist congressional candidate, rival to veteran representative Adriano Espaillat |url= https://www.diariolasamericas.com/eeuu/mamdani-respalda-candidata-socialista-al-congreso-rival-del-veterano-representante-adriano-espaillat-n5396303 |publisher=[[Diario Las Américas]] |access-date=June 1, 2026 |language=es-US}}</ref> and speaks fluent [[Spanish language|Spanish]].<ref name="CityState2026Pretsky">{{Cite web |last=Pretsky |first= Holly |date=June 15, 2026 |title=Like AOC, but to the left |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/personality/2026/06/like-aoc-but-left/414164/ |access-date=June 16, 2026 |website= City & State NY |language=en}}</ref> Her maternal grandfather was a member of the resistance movement against Dominican dictator [[Rafael Trujillo]] and his successor [[Joaquín Balaguer]], leading the family to emigrate to the US.<ref name="TheCity2026Aponte">{{cite news |last1=Aponte |first1=Claudia Irizarry |title=DSA's Endorsement of Darializa Avila Chevalier Poses Test of Its Clout |url=https://www.thecity.nyc/2026/01/27/dsas-endorsement-of-darializa-avila-chevalier-poses-test-of-its-clout/ |access-date=February 7, 2026 |publisher=[[The City (website)|The City]] |date=January 27, 2026}}</ref><ref name="HellGate2026Staff" />

Avila Chevalier spent her childhood in [[Miami]], and many of her teenage years in [[Tallahassee]], where she attended Hartsfield Elementary School and Fairview Middle School, graduating from [[James S. Rickards High School]] in 2012.<ref name="WadeInTheWaterChevalier">{{cite news |title=Darializa Avila-Chevalier (interview) |url=http://wadezine.com/interviews/darializa-avila-chevalier.html |access-date=February 7, 2026 |work=Wade in the Water}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=McCoy Vann |first1=Kim |title=Lights! Camera! Talk books! |url= https://www.newspapers.com/article/tallahassee-democrat-lights-camera-tal/200246914/ |access-date=June 24, 2026 |via=Newspapers.com |work=Tallahassee Democrat |date=November 23, 2004 |pages=1B, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/tallahassee-democrat-stars/200247016/ 2B]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Gold Stars; Students win Science Olympiad |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/tallahassee-democrat-gold-stars-student/200231805/ |access-date=June 24, 2026 |via=Newspapers.com |work=Tallahassee Democrat |date=October 25, 2005 |page=2B}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Rickards Graduates |url= https://www.newspapers.com/article/tallahassee-democrat-rickards-graduates/200246634/ |access-date=June 24, 2026 |via=Newspapers.com |work=Tallahassee Democrat |date=May 16, 2012 |page=39}}</ref>

Avila Chevalier moved to [[New York City]] to study at [[Columbia College, Columbia University]],<ref name= "AmsterdamNews2025Long" /><ref name= "ColumbiaSpectator2026Lee" /> where she was an illustrator for the ''[[Columbia Daily Spectator]]''.<ref>{{cite AV media |title= Darializa's story |date=May 15, 2024 |time= 0:10 |publisher= [[Latino USA]] |url= https://soundcloud.com/latinousa/darializas-story}}</ref> She graduated in 2016 with a Bachelor of Arts in [[Middle Eastern studies]].<ref name= "WadeInTheWaterChevalier" />

As a student at Columbia College, Avila Chevalier organized with [[Students for Justice in Palestine]] and Mobilized African Diaspora.<ref name= "WadeInTheWaterChevalier" /> In 2014 Avila Chevalier lived in the Palestinian city of [[Nablus]] for around two months while interning for [[Tomorrow's Youth Organization]] to teach English to Palestinian toddlers and children. The [[2014 Gaza War]] started shortly after she returned to the US.<ref name= "CityState2026Pretsky" /> She credited this period with shaping her view that the oppression of Palestinians is directly linked to the American system, saying, "these are not only ''like'' systems, they are the ''same'' system. It was the same tear gas made in the USA that was being dropped on Gaza that was also being used against [[Black Lives Matter]] protesters [[Ferguson unrest|in Ferguson]]."<ref name= "CityState2026Pretsky" /> She co-founded student organization [[Columbia University Apartheid Divest]],<ref>{{Cite web |last= Fund |first= John |date= June 24, 2026|title= The rise and rise of America's radical left |url= https://spectator.com/article/the-rise-and-rise-of-americas-radical-left/ |website= [[The Spectator]] |language= en-US}}</ref> helping establish it in 2016.<ref name="JTA2026Strauss" />

Avila Chevalier began a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] program in [[sociology]] at the [[CUNY Graduate Center|Graduate School and University Center]] of the [[City University of New York]],<ref name= "USAToday2025Avila">{{cite news |last1= Avila Chevalier |first1= Darializa |date= March 13, 2025 |title= I worked alongside Mahmoud Khalil. His detention is a terrifying abuse of power. |url= https://usatoday.com/story/opinion/voices/2025/03/13/columbia-university-ice-detention-mahmoud-khalil/82316469007/ |access-date= February 8, 2026 |publisher= [[USA Today]]}}</ref> becoming a [[All but dissertation|doctoral candidate]] by 2025.<ref name= "USAToday2025Avila" /> Her research has focused on [[List of United States immigration and nationality laws|immigration law]] and [[Immigration policy of the United States|policy]] and [[incarceration in the United States]], especially on the ways Black immigrants from [[Latin America]] have been affected by the US criminal justice system and deportation.<ref name= "CUNYJohnJay">{{cite web |title= Darializa Avila Chevalier |url= https://www.sadrjohnjay.com/artists/darializa-avila-chevalier-ml9am |access-date= February 7, 2026 |website= Social Anatomy of a Deportation Regime |publisher= John Jay College of Criminal Justice, [[CUNY]]}}</ref>

== Early career and activism ==
===Black Youth Project 100===
{{see|Black Youth Project 100}}
After graduating from Columbia, Avila Chevalier organized with the [[Black Youth Project 100]].<ref name= "Jacobin2026Day" /> In 2018, the group demanded removal of a [[Central Park]] statue of [[J. Marion Sims]], a 19th-century gynecologist who forcibly subjected enslaved Black women to experiments involving painful surgical techniques without anesthesia, despite later administering anesthesia to his white patients.<ref name= "AmericanProspect2025Wimbish">{{cite news |last1=Wimbish |first1= Whitney Curry |title= Justice Dems Pick Longtime Organizer to Take Harlem |url= https://prospect.org/2025/11/20/darializa-avila-chevalier-harlem-new-york-city-congress-justice-dems/ |access-date= February 7, 2026 |publisher= [[The American Prospect]] |date= November 20, 2025}}</ref> Avila Chevalier and three other Black women protested in front of the statue dressed in blood-stained hospital gowns, reading passages from Sims's autobiography, medical journals, and other historical material that highlighted his dehumanization of enslaved women.<ref>{{cite news |last1= Escalante |first1= Alejandro S. |title= Gynecology and the Ungendering of Black Women |url= https://www.aaihs.org/gynecology-and-the-ungendering-of-black-women/ |access-date= February 8, 2026 |publisher= African American Intellectual Historical Society |date=December 4, 2018}}</ref> The statue was moved later that year.<ref>{{cite news |last1= Domonoske |first1= Camila | title= 'Father Of Gynecology,' Who Experimented On Slaves, No Longer On Pedestal In NYC |access-date= June 3, 2026 |publisher= NPR |date= April 17, 2018 |url= https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2018/04/17/603163394/-father-of-gynecology-who-experimented-on-slaves-no-longer-on-pedestal-in-nyc}}</ref>

===Families for Freedom===
In 2019, as an organizer for Families for Freedom, Avila Chevalier protested to free Abdikadir Mohamed Felt, a Somali immigrant affected by President [[Donald Trump]]'s "[[Executive Order 13769|Muslim ban]]", from [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) detention.<ref>{{cite web |last1= Hussain |first1= Murtaza |title= His Visa Was Stamped, His Papers in Order. Then He Was Targeted By a Secretive CBP Task Force. |url= https://theintercept.com/2019/05/13/customs-border-protection-profiling-airport/ |website= The Intercept |date= May 13, 2019}}</ref> She later published an analysis of the convergence of US counterterrorism policy and immigration enforcement as exemplified by the emergence of [[United States Customs and Border Protection]]'s (CBP) units known as Tactical Terrorism Response Teams, with Abdikadir Mohamed's encounter with such a unit serving as a [[case study]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last= Avila Chevalier |first= Darializa |date=July 3, 2023 |title= The securitisation of immigration through the Tactical Terrorism Response Team |url= https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/17539153.2023.2229618 |journal= Critical Studies on Terrorism |language= en |volume=16 |issue=3 |pages= 537–559 |doi= 10.1080/17539153.2023.2229618 |issn= 1753-9153|url-access= subscription }}</ref>

[[File:Columbia reinstated Gaza Solidarity Encampment, day 5, 4x5 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Avila Chevalier participated in the [[Gaza Solidarity Encampment (Columbia University)|Gaza Solidarity Encampment]] (April 17–30, 2024), part of the [[Columbia University pro-Palestinian campus protests during the Gaza war|Columbia University protests]] against the [[Gaza war]] and [[Gaza genocide|genocide]].]]

As an alumna, Avila Chevalier participated in the April 2024 [[Gaza Solidarity Encampment (Columbia University)|Gaza Solidarity Encampment]],<ref>{{Cite web |last= Lee |first= Katharine |title= Darializa Avila Chevalier, CC '16, Eli Northrup, Jordan Wright win primaries in West Harlem |url= https://www.columbiaspectator.com/city-news/2026/06/24/darializa-avila-chevalier-eli-northrup-jordan-wright-win-primaries-in-west-harlem/ |access-date= June 28, 2026 |website= Columbia Daily Spectator}}</ref> part of the [[Columbia University pro-Palestinian campus protests during the Gaza war|protests at Columbia University]] demanding that the university officially call for a ceasefire and [[disinvestment from Israel|disinvest from Israel]] during the [[Gaza war|war]] and [[Gaza genocide|genocide]] in Gaza,<ref name= "CityState2026Sterne">{{cite news |last1= Sterne |first1= Peter |title= DSA votes to endorse Espaillat challenger Darializa Avila Chevalier |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/01/dsa-votes-endorse-espaillat-challenger-darializa-avila-chevalier/410884/ |access-date= February 7, 2026 |publisher= [[City and State New York]] |date= January 22, 2026}}</ref><ref name= "Time2024Mansoor">{{Cite news |last=Mansoor |first= Sanya |date= April 29, 2024 |title= 'Gaza Calls, Columbia Falls': Campus Protesters Defy Suspension Threats and Occupy Hall |url= https://time.com/6972454/columbia-protesters-defy-university-orders-to-clear-encampment/ |work= [[Time Magazine]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1= Pinto |first1= Nick |last2= Ang |first2= Angelica |date= April 30, 2024 |title= Columbia's Student Protesters Are Still Schooling the Administration |url= https://hellgatenyc.com/columbia-student-protesters-still-schooling-the-administration/ |work= Hellgate NYC |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240501075710/https://hellgatenyc.com/columbia-student-protesters-still-schooling-the-administration/ |archive-date= May 1, 2024 |access-date= May 12, 2026}}</ref><ref name= "ColumbiaSpectator2026Lee">{{Cite web |last= Lee |first= Katharine |date= April 26, 2026 |title= Race for Rep. Adriano Espaillat's congressional seat draws legal objections from multiple campaigns |url= https://www.columbiaspectator.com/city-news/2026/04/26/race-for-rep-adriano-espaillats-congressional-seat-draws-legal-objections-from-multiple-campaigns/ |access-date= June 1, 2026 |website= [[Columbia Daily Spectator]]}}</ref><ref name= "NYTimes2026Goldenberg">{{Cite news |last1= Goldenberg |first1= Sally |last2= King |first2= Maya |date= May 28, 2026 |title= Mamdani Vowed to Back Espaillat. Now He's Endorsing a D.S.A. Challenger. |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/28/nyregion/adriano-espaillat-darializa-avila-chevalier-mamdani.html |access-date= June 1, 2026 |work= The New York Times |language= en-US |issn= 0362-4331}}</ref> for which she was targeted by [[Canary Mission]], a pro-[[Israel]] [[doxing]] website.<ref name= "Jacobin2026Day">{{cite news |last1= Day |first1= Meagan |title= In Harlem, a Democratic Socialist Takes On the Dem Machine |url= https://jacobin.com/2026/01/avila-chevalier-harlem-bronx-socialism |work= [[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]] |access-date= February 7, 2026 |date= January 21, 2026}}</ref>

In November 2023, when Columbia [[Columbia University pro-Palestinian campus protests during the Gaza war#November 10, 2023: Students for Justice in Palestine and Jewish Voice for Peace irregularly suspended|suspended]] its chapters of [[Students for Justice in Palestine]] and [[Jewish Voice for Peace]], Avila Chevalier said the university should "protect speech and protect the right of faculty and students to address these issues in an open and frank way".<ref>{{Cite web |date= November 15, 2023 |title= Hundreds protest at Columbia over school's decision to suspend student groups calling for cease-fire |url= https://abc7ny.com/post/columbia-university-protests-israel-palestine/14064751/ |access-date= June 2, 2026 |website= ABC7 New York |language= en}}</ref> On April 30, 2024, [[Strategic Response Group (New York City Police Department)|riot police]] forcibly removed protesters, including Avila Chevalier from the entrance to [[Hamilton Hall (Columbia University)|Hamilton Hall]]. Avila Chevalier said that officers pushed her and other protesters to the floor, leaving them with bruises.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last= Mansoor |first= Sanya |date= May 1, 2024 |title= Inside Columbia and City College's Darkest Night |url= https://time.com/6973166/columbia-university-city-college-pro-palestinian-protests-arrests/ |access-date= June 19, 2026 |magazine= TIME |language= en}}</ref>

=== Career ===
Avila Chevalier has taught at CUNY [[Lehman College]] and [[New York University]].<ref name="CityState2026Pretsky" />

She works as an investigator at the [[public defender]] legal organization Neighborhood Defender Service of Harlem,<ref name="AmericanProspect2025Wimbish" /> where she is a member of the Association of Legal Aid Attorneys – [[United Auto Workers]] Local 2325.<ref name="NYTimes2025King">{{cite news |last1=King |first1=Maya |title=Justice Democrats Re-Emerge in New York to Try to Unseat Espaillat |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/20/nyregion/justice-democrats-espaillat-avila-chevalier.html |access-date= February 7, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=November 20, 2025}}</ref><ref name="TheCity2025Aponte">{{cite news |last1=Aponte |first1=Claudia Irizarry |last2=Samuel|first2=Marina|title=Union Members Take On Congressional Incumbents in Manhattan and The Bronx |url=https://www.thecity.nyc/2025/11/24/avila-chevalier-nemorin-espaillat-torres-bronx-congress-uaw/ |access-date=February 7, 2026 |publisher=[[The City (website)|The City]] |date= November 24, 2025}}</ref> Her work has investigated [[police brutality in the United States]].<ref name="DiarioLasAmericas2026" />

Avila Chevalier ran in the Democratic primary for [[New York's 13th congressional district]], challenging incumbent [[Adriano Espaillat]], chair of the [[Congressional Hispanic Caucus]], who has represented the district since 2017.<ref name="NYTimes2026Goldenberg" /><ref name="Axios2025Solender">{{cite news |last=Solender |first= Andrew |date=November 20, 2025 |title=Hispanic Caucus chair becomes latest House Democrat to draw a primary foe |url= https://www.axios.com/2025/11/20/adriano-espaillat-primary-challenge-darializa |work=Axios |access-date= June 21, 2026}}</ref><ref name= "HuffPost2025">{{Cite web |last=Robillard |first=Kevin |date=November 20, 2025 |title= Mamdani's Win Is Inspiring A Wave Of Left-Wing Challengers In NYC |url= https://www.huffpost.com/entry/mamdanis-win-is-inspiring-a-wave-of-left-wing-challengers-in-nyc_n_691e7ba1e4b0d33fcd986732 |website=HuffPost}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Solis |first=Marcus |date=June https://abc7ny.com/post/adriano-espaillat-darializa-avila-chevalier-face-off-race-nys-13th-congressional-district/19326394/ |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website=ABC7 New York |language=en}}</ref> NY-13 encompasses [[Harlem]] and the southwest section of [[the Bronx]] and is one of the most Democratic districts in the country.<ref name= "NYTimes2026Goldenberg" /> At 32, she would be one of the youngest members of Congress.<ref>{{cite news |last1= Daniels |first1= Cheyanne |date= January 25, 2026 |title= The rift over generational change roils the Congressional Black Caucus |url= https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/25/congressional-black-caucus-2026-midterms-00741618 |publisher=[[Politico]]}}</ref> Avila Chevalier was the only challenger to outraise an incumbent in New York City during the first quarter of 2026.<ref name= TheCityReporter2026Irizarry>{{cite news |last= Aponte |first= Claudia Irizarry |date=May 15, 2026 |title= Espaillat Ramps Up Efforts to Fend Off DSA-Backed Challenger |url= https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/05/15/espaillat-avila-chevalier-primary-ny13/ |access-date=May 29, 2026 |publisher= [[The City (website)|The City]]}}</ref> An April 2026 internal campaign poll showed her trailing Espaillat by 18 percentage points after voters were read biographical statements about both candidates.<ref name="TheCity2026ApontePoll">{{cite news |last=Aponte |first=Claudia Irizarry |date= April 20, 2026 |title= DSA-Backed Challenger Says She's Gaining on Rep. Adriano Espaillat |url= https://www.thecity.nyc/2026/04/20/espaillat-poll-darializa-avila-chevalier-ny13/ |access-date=June 21, 2026 |publisher= [[The City (website)|The City]]}}</ref>

Avila Chevalier was recruited to run by [[Justice Democrats]],<ref name="NYTimes2025King" /><ref name= TheCityReporter2026Irizarry /><ref>{{cite web |title=Endorsed Candidates |url= https://justicedemocrats.com/candidates/ |publisher=Justice Democrats |access-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref><ref name= "HellGate2026Staff" /> who previously helped Ocasio-Cortez win [[2018 New York's 14th congressional district election|her 2018 election]] against an incumbent.<ref name="Axios2026Solender" /> Avila Chevalier was endorsed by New York mayor [[Zohran Mamdani]],<ref name="Axios2026Solender">{{cite news |last=Solender |first= Andrew |date= May 29, 2026 |title= House's top Hispanic Dem is in a fight for his political life |url= https://www.axios.com/2026/05/29/adriano-espaillat-darializa-avila-chevalier-ny |work=Axios |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260610032719/https://www.axios.com/2026/05/29/adriano-espaillat-darializa-avila-chevalier-ny |archive-date=June 10, 2026 |access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Oreskes |first= Benjamin |date=June 4, 2026 |title=We Interrupt This Knicks Victory for a Political Ad Starring Mamdani |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/03/nyregion/mamdani-knicks-ad-campaign.html |access-date=June 5, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name="ElDiario2026">{{Cite web |last=Martinez |first=Edwin |date=May 29, 2026 |title=Mamdani anuncia respaldo a Darializa Avila para llegar al Congreso: 'Hay que abolir a ICE' |url=https://eldiariony.com/2026/05/29/mamdani-anuncia-respaldo-a-darializa-avila-para-llegar-al-congreso-hay-que-abolir-a-ice/ |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website=El Diario NY |language=es-US}}</ref><ref name="MSNow2026">{{Cite web |last=Herreria |first=Carla |date=May 29, 2026 |title=Mamdani endorses democratic socialist challenging Rep. Adriano Espaillat |url=https://www.ms.now/news/mamdani-endorses-democratic-socialist-challenging-rep-adriano-espaillat |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website=MS Now}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Prater |first=Nia |date=May 29, 2026 |title=Mamdani's Highest-Stakes Endorsement Yet |url= https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/mamdanis-highest-stakes-endorsement-yet.html |website=Intelligencer |access-date= June 21, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergin |first=Brigid |date=May 29, 2026 |title=Mayor Mamdani flexes political power with endorsement of Espaillat challenger |url=https://gothamist.com/news/mayor-mamdani-flexes-political-power-with-endorsement-of-espaillat-challenger |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website=[[Gothamist]] |language=en}}</ref> [[United Auto Workers]] Region 9A,<ref name="UAW2026">{{cite web |title=NYC CAP Announces Third Round of 2026 Endorsements |url=https://region9a.uaw.org/news/NYCEndorsements426 |publisher=UAW Region 9A |access-date=April 19, 2026 |language=en |date=April 17, 2026}}</ref> the [[New York City Democratic Socialists of America]],<ref name="TheCity2026Aponte" /><ref name="CityState2026Donaldson">{{Cite web |last=Donaldson |first=Sahalie |date=April 27, 2026 |title=DSA is targeting Rep. Adriano Espaillat in NY-13 |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/04/dsa-targeting-rep-adriano-espaillat-ny-13/413110/ |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website=City & State NY}}</ref> and [[Jewish Voice for Peace]] Action.<ref name= "AmsterdamNews2025Long" /> She was also supported by former US representative [[Jamaal Bowman]]<ref name= "AmsterdamNews2025Long" /> and political commentator [[Hasan Piker]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Steakin |first=William |date= June 4, 2026 |title=Hasan Piker declares 'I'm not a kingmaker' after his candidates struggle |url= https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/04/hasan-piker-democratic-primaries-00949340 |access-date=June 24, 2026 |website= [[Politico]] |language=en}}</ref>

Outside groups spent heavily in the race. The Congressional Hispanic Caucus's political arm spent to support Espaillat,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pretsky |first=Holly |date=June 16, 2026 |title=Super PACs have spent millions boosting Adriano Espaillat and Darializa Avila Chevalier. Both candidates think that's super hypocritical! |url= |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Solender |first=Andrew |date=June 11, 2026 |title=Hispanic Caucus spending "heavily" to save its chair from Mamdani-backed challenger |url= https://www.axios.com/2026/06/11/espaillat-darializa-chevalier-new-york-hispanic |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website= Axios |language=en}}</ref> and [[AIPAC]] spent at least $650,000 opposing Avila Chevalier;<ref name="CityState2026SterneAIPAC">{{cite news |last=Sterne |first=Peter |date=June 20, 2026 |title=AIPAC is helping boost Espaillat against DSA https://web.archive.org/web/20260621035730/https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/aipac-helping-boost-espaillat-against-dsa-challenge/414300/ |archive-date=June 21, 2026 |access-date=June 21, 2026}}</ref> AIPAC-associated donors also spent to support Espaillat.<ref name="JewishCurrentsAntiAIPAC">{{Cite web |last= Kane |first= Alex |date= June 11, 2026 |title= An Anti-AIPAC Insurgent Tests Her Message in a Working-Class Stronghold |url= https://jewishcurrents.org/an-anti-aipac-insurgent-tests-her-message-in-a-working-class-stronghold |access-date= June 21, 2026 |website=Jewish Currents |language=en}}</ref><ref name="DropSite2026">{{cite web |last1=Grim |first1= Ryan |last2=Andreone |first2=Julian |date=June 16, 2026 |title=Pro-Israel Donors Power Last-Minute Surge of Espaillat https://web.archive.org/web/20260616004540/https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/pro-israel-donors-aipac-adriano-espaillat-avila-chevalier |archive-date=June 16, 2026 |access-date=June 21, 2026}}</ref>

Espaillat retained support from several progressive Democrats, including [[Congressional Progressive Caucus]] chair [[Greg Casar]].<ref>{{cite news |last1= Beeferman |first1= Jason |last2= Fernandez |first2= Madison |last3= Reisman |first3= Nick |last4= Sommerfeldt |first4= Chris |title= Progressives for Espaillat |url= https://www.politico.com/newsletters/new-york-playbook/2026/05/14/progressives-for-espaillat-00920155 |access-date= June 21, 2026 |date= May 14, 2026 |website= [[Politico]]}}</ref> The [[Congressional Black Caucus]] also backed him in the primary.<ref>{{cite news |last= Beeferman |first= Jason |date= January 15, 2026 |title= Congressional Black Caucus backs Espaillat in primary |url= https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/15/congressional-black-caucus-espaillat-primary-00728543 |access-date= June 21, 2026 |website= [[Politico]]}}</ref> The race highlighted tensions between the Democratic Party's "establishment" wing and its democratic socialists.<ref>{{cite news |last= Silva |first= Manuela |date= June 19, 2026 |title= This New York Race Is a Microcosm of Democrats' Identity Fight |url= https://www.notus.org/2026-election/darializa-avila-chevalier-adriano-espaillat-primary |website= Notus |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260621222240/https://www.notus.org/2026-election/darializa-avila-chevalier-adriano-espaillat-primary |archive-date= June 21, 2026 |access-date= June 21, 2026}}</ref> Espaillat called Avila Chevalier's [[democratic socialism]] a "failed ideology".<ref>{{cite news |last= Bergin |first= Brigid |date= June 4, 2026 |title= From Insurgent to Establishment: Rep. Espaillat Reckons With Uptown's Shift to the Left |url= https://gothamist.com/news/from-insurgent-to-establishment-rep-espaillat-reckons-with-uptown-shift-to-the-left |work= [[Gothamist]] |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260604105237/https://gothamist.com/news/from-insurgent-to-establishment-rep-espaillat-reckons-with-uptown-shift-to-the-left |archive-date= June 4, 2026 |access-date= June 21, 2026}}</ref>

During the campaign, Avila Chevalier faced criticism and controversy regarding her background. ''City & State'' reported that Rusking Pimentel, a senior adviser to Espaillat, made comments about Avila Chevalier that were characterized as racist and Islamophobic in Spanish-language media.<ref name=":32">{{Cite web |last= Sterne |first= Peter |date=June 22, 2026 |title= Espaillat senior adviser made racist and Islamophobic comments about congressional challenger |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/espaillat-senior-adviser-made-racist-and-islamophobic-comments-about-congressional-challenger/414333/ |access-date= June 24, 2026 |website= City & State NY |language=en}}</ref> Some Espailiat supporters publicly questioned her ties to the Dominican community in New York City, incorrectly identifying her as Haitian.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":32" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mays |first= Jeffery C. |date= June 23, 2026 |title= Ethnicity Becomes Instrument of Division in Espaillat's Re-election Bid |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/23/nyregion/darializa-avila-chevalier-dominican-haiti.html |access-date=June 24, 2026 |work= The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In a separate exchange, Espailiat called some Avila Chevalier supporters "gentrifiers" who, he said, contributed to rising rents. Avila Chevalier has advocated for federal funding to support the development of social housing.<ref name= "CityState2026SterneSpar">{{cite news |last=Sterne |first=Peter |date=June 20, 2026 |title= Espaillat, Avila Chevalier spar over gentrification in Harlem church |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/espaillat-avila-chevalier-spar-over-gentrification-harlem-church/414301/ |work= City & State New York |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260621063435/https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/espaillat-avila-chevalier-spar-over-gentrification-harlem-church/414301/ |archive-date= June 21, 2026 |access-date= June 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

News media and Espaillat scrutinized [[Tweet (social media)|tweets]] Avila Chevalier made from a [[Twitter, Inc.|Twitter]] account she used from 2018 to 2022. She said she deleted the account before Twitter was [[Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk|acquired by Elon Musk]] to focus on her studies and on organizing.<ref name=":3">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mncXnjrNGAA |title='Abandonment from establishment politics': Darializa Avila Chevalier confronts the scrutiny against |date=June 24, 2026 |last=MS NOW |access-date=July 8, 2026 |via=YouTube|minutes=2:39}}</ref> In her tweets, Avila Chevalier criticized mainstream [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]], calling [[Joe Biden]] "a rapist" in 2020, though she later said she voted for him in [[2020 United States presidential election|that year's presidential election]].<ref name="NY12026Staff2">{{Cite web |date=May 29, 2026 |title=Why Darializa Avila Chevalier wants to challenge Rep. Espaillat |url= https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/inside-city-hall/2026/05/29/why-darializa-avila-chevalier-wants-to-challenge-rep--espaillat |access-date=June 2, 2026 |website=NY1 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="CNN2026Kaczynski">{{cite news |last1=Kaczynski |first1=Andrew |last2=Steck |first2=Em |date=June 1, 2026 |title=Mamdani-backed congressional candidate deleted posts calling to seize private property, abolish police, borders, prisons |url= https://us.cnn.com/2026/06/01/politics/kfile-ny-13-darializa-avila-chevalier-deleted-tweets-defund-abolish-police-prisons-deportations |access-date=June 2, 2026 |work=[[CNN]]}}</ref><ref name= "NYTimes2026June14Goldenberg">{{cite web |last1=Goldenberg |first1=Sally |last2=King |first2=Maya |date=June 14, 2026 |title=Tweet, Delete, Repeat: Social Media Posts Overshadow N.Y. House Race |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/14/nyregion/avila-chevalier-social-media.html |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website= The New York Times}}</ref><ref name="cnn_tweets">{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=David |date=June 17, 2026 |title= A Mamdani-backed progressive's challenge to a veteran Democrat highlights party fractures |url= https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/17/politics/ny-13-darializa-avila-chevalier-kamala-harris |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website= CNN |language= en}}</ref> She tweeted "fuck [[Kamala Harris]]" in 2021 after Harris gave a speech discouraging migration to the US,<ref name= "NYTimes2026June14Goldenberg"/> but apologized publicly to Harris during a debate.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |last1= Pretsky |first1= Holly |last2= Donaldson |first2= Sahalie |last3= Lewis |first3= Rebecca C. |title= Darializa Avila Chevalier upsets Rep. Adriano Espaillat |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/darializa-avila-chevalier-upsets-rep-adriano-espaillat/414375/ |website= City & State NY |access-date= June 29, 2026 |language=en |date= June 24, 2026}}</ref> She later said her posts came from a sense of political disempowerment felt by many Americans.<ref name= "cnn_tweets"/><ref name= "detzel_msnow">{{Cite web| last= Detzel| first= Allison|title= Chevalier says she 'regrets' controversial social media posts that caused 'division'|work=[[MSNOW]]|date=June 25, 2026| url= https://www.ms.now/news/darializa-avila-chevalier-new-york-primary-regrets-old-social-media-harris-biden| access-date= June 28, 2026}}</ref>

In other tweets, she advocated [[prison abolition]], [[police abolition]], and [[border abolition]]. She rejected the [[Legitimacy of the State of Israel|view that Israel has a "right to exist"]] as a Jewish state.<ref name="NY12026Staff2" /><ref name="CNN2026Kaczynski" /><ref name="NYTimes2026June14Goldenberg" /><ref name="cnn_tweets" /> Other tweets related to communism, COVID-19, and interracial relationships.{{efn|One of her posts in 2019 supported the seizure of the [[means of production]]. Her repost called for [[nationalization]] of [[pharmaceutical companies]], [[hospital]]s and [[landlord]]s' property.<ref name="CNN2026Kaczynski" /> Avila Chevalier's tweets from 2020 to 2022 contained various references to [[communism]] and [[Marxism]]. One of her [[retweet]]s recommended that people read [[Karl Marx]]'s ''[[Das Kapital]]''.<ref>{{Cite news |last= Kaczynski |first= Andrew |date= June 29, 2026 |title= Deleted tweets on Darializa Avila Chevalier's account had favorable references to communist leaders and Marxism |url= https://edition.cnn.com/2026/06/29/politics/darializa-avila-chevalier-communism-tweets |work= [[CNN Politics]] |language= en}}</ref> In a May 2020 tweet, she called [[COVID-19]] a "European plague" and boosted a post suggesting the [[Origin of SARS-CoV-2|virus originated]] in [[France]] rather than [[Wuhan, China]]. She also criticized "Black" and "Arab men" for "fetishizing ugly colonizer women".<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite web| last1= MITTELSTADT |first1= NATALIA |title= Mamdani-backed House candidate's deleted posts called for abolishing police, borders |url= https://cbs12.com/news/nation-world/mamdani-backed-house-candidates-deleted-posts-called-for-abolishing-police-borders-democratic-socialist-nyc-adriano-espaillat-primary-blm-bernie-sanders-aoc-joe-biden |website= WPEC |access-date= June 29, 2026 |language= en |date= June 2, 2026}}</ref> In another tweet she responded to a prompt of "interracial relationship discourse, go" with a celebratory image, followed by "No yts tho" and an emoji. ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[The Washington Post]]'' suggested this disparaged [[interracial relationships]] involving [[White people]].<ref name="wp-binday">{{cite news |last1= Binday |first1= Ben |title= Democratic socialist won N.Y. primary despite scrutiny over inflammatory posts |url= https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/06/24/darializa-avila-chevalier-scrutinized-posts-before-new-york-house-primary-win/ |newspaper= [[The Washington Post]] |access-date= July 2, 2026 |date= June 24, 2026}}</ref><ref name= "NYTimes2026June14Goldenberg" />}} In reference to its focus on Avila Chevalier's tweets, [[Mehdi Hasan]] accused ''[[The New York Times]]'' of applying more scrutiny to her than to right-wing figures.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Take: Mehdi Hasan: Disrupting democracy's decline |url= https://www.aljazeera.com/podcasts/2026/6/29/the-take-mehdi-hasan-disrupting-democracys-decline |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zeteo |first=Team |title=Mehdi vs. the New York Times |url=https://zeteo.com/p/mehdi-vs-the-new-york-times |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=zeteo.com |language=en}}</ref> She responded to coverage of her posts by saying, "I was young, yes, and I was a millennial with internet access", and added that the attention was "litigating the politics of the past instead of the politics of the future and the present".<ref name="NY12026Staff2" /> Avila Chevalier said she regrets her past Twitter activity due to the division it caused.<ref name=":3" /><ref name="detzel_msnow" /> Mamdani reiterated his endorsement of her campaign after the report, citing her ongoing advocacy for immigrants and working-class New Yorkers.<ref name="CNN2026Kaczynski" />

Avila Chevalier defeated Espaillat in the Democratic primary in an [[Upset (competition)|upset]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Bowman |first1= Bridget |last2= Kamisar |first2= Ben |date= June 24, 2026 |title= Democratic Rep. Adriano Espaillat loses primary to Mamdani-backed Darializa Avila Chevalier |url= https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/espaillat-ny-house-primary-loss-district-13-avila-chevalier-rcna351127 |access-date= June 24, 2026 |website= NBC News |language= en}}</ref> According to incomplete returns, she won 49.4% of the vote to his 45.9%; she won younger voters by 24%, college-educated voters by 20%, higher-income voters by 6%, and black voters by 2%. Espaillat won lower-income voters by 10% and Hispanic voters by 16%.<ref>{{cite web |title=New York 13th Congressional District Primary Election Results |url= https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/us/elections/results-new-york-us-house-13-primary.html |website= nytimes.com |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=20 July 2026}}</ref> If elected in November, Avila Chevalier will be the first socialist to represent the district since [[Vito Marcantonio]] in the 1950s.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Fund |first1= John |date=June 24, 2026 |title= The rise and rise of America's radical left |url= https://spectator.com/article/the-rise-and-rise-of-americas-radical-left/?edition=us |access-date=June 24, 2026 |website= [[The Spectator]] |language= en}}</ref>

== Political positions ==
Avila Chevalier is a political [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rogerson |first1=Riley |title=Will the Hispanic Caucus welcome Darializa Avila Chevalier? |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/25/darializa-avila-chevalier-espaillat-chc-00977027 |website=POLITICO |access-date=June 29, 2026 |language=en |date=June 25, 2026}}</ref> and [[Democratic socialism|democratic socialist]],<ref name="wp-binday" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=King |first=Maya |date=June 24, 2026 |title=Darializa Avila Chevalier, a Mamdani Ally, Ousts Espaillat in Primary |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/23/nyregion/ny13-darializa-avila-chevalier-espaillat.html |access-date=June 25, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Solender |first=Andrew |date=June 24, 2026 |title=Congressional Hispanic Caucus chair unseated by socialist challenger |url= https://www.axios.com/2026/06/24/espaillat-darializa-chevalier-ny-13-results |access-date=June 25, 2026 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=David| date= June 17, 2026 |title= A Mamdani-backed progressive's challenge to a veteran Democrat highlights party fractures {{!}} CNN Politics |url= https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/17/politics/ny-13-darializa-avila-chevalier-kamala-harris |access-date=June 25, 2026 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Gómez |first1=Fin Daniel| last2= Linton |first2= Caroline |last3= Yilek |first3= Caitlin |last4= Hudak |first4= Zak |date= June 24, 2026| title= Political earthquake strikes House Democrats and Hispanic caucus with Espaillat's loss |url= https://www.cbsnews.com/news/adriano-espaillat-loss-congressional-hispanic-caucus-darializa-avila-chevalier/ |access-date= June 25, 2026 |website=CBS News |language=en-US}}</ref> and ''The New York Times'' has characterized her views as [[far-left]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldenberg |first1=Sally |title=Avila Chevalier Won Despite Far-Left Views. Will They Hurt Democrats? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/24/nyregion/avila-chevalier-espaillat.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=June 28, 2026 |date=June 25, 2026}}</ref> In an interview with [[MS NOW]], she said she is not a [[Communism|communist]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Stanton |first=Zack |date=June 30, 2026 |title=Avila Chevalier, after primary upset, says she is not a communist |url=https://www.ms.now/news/darializa-avila-chevalier-dsa-communist |access-date=July 3, 2026 |website=MS NOW |language=en-US}}</ref> Avila Chevalier opposes all forms of [[deportation]] as well as [[United States support for Israel in the Gaza war|US support for Israel]] during the [[Gaza war|war]] and [[Gaza genocide|genocide]] in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Jacobin2026Day" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Denvir |first=Daniel |date=June 18, 2026 |title=Darializa Avila Chevalier on Running for Congress in Zohran's NYC |url=https://jacobin.com/2026/06/avila-chevalier-espaillat-nyc-socialism |access-date=June 21, 2026 |website=[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Her platform has included universal healthcare, stronger tenant protections, funding programs for children instead of funding war, abolishing [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|US Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE), banning large [[Political action committee#Super PACs|super PACs]] from elections, and prohibiting members of Congress from trading stocks.<ref name="Guardian2026Sainato">{{Cite news |last=Sainato |first=Michael |date=June 22, 2026 |title=Progressive New Yorker backed by Zohran Mamdani for US Congress targets 'establishment' |url= https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jun/22/darializa-avila-chevalier-new-york-zohran-mamdani |access-date= June 30, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref name="Guardian2026Speri">{{Cite news |last=Speri |first=Alice |date=June 24, 2026 |title=Darializa Avila Chevalier: pro-Palestinian doctoral student steps into politics with 'faith in the future' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jun/24/darializa-avila-chevalier-win-new-york |access-date=June 30, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

Avila Chevalier is a member of the [[New York City Democratic Socialists of America]] (NYC-DSA),<ref name= "Jacobin2026Day"/><ref name= "HellGate2026Staff" /> which she joined in 2025.<ref name= "CityState2026Pretsky" /> She has described her political views as having been informed by the [[Black radical tradition]], specifically the writings of [[Angela Davis]] and [[Assata Shakur]],<ref name= "Jacobin2026Day" /> as well as her experience in Palestine in 2014.<ref name="CityState2026Pretsky" /> In the [[2025 New York City mayoral election]], Avila Chevalier was an organizing lead on DSA member [[Zohran Mamdani]]'s campaign.<ref name= "AmsterdamNews2025Long"/><ref name= "Jacobin2026Day"/><ref name="NYTimes2025King"/><ref name= "TheCity2025Aponte"/> She ranked [[Brad Lander]] fifth on her ballot in protest of his comments about [[Mahmoud Khalil]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= Coltin |first= Jeff |date= March 12, 2026 |title= Why Espaillat challenger Chevalier ranked Lander fifth for mayor |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/03/why-espaillat-challenger-chevalier-ranked-lander-fifth-mayor/412069/ |access-date= June 5, 2026 |website= City & State NY |language= en}}</ref>

On April 13, 2026, Avila Chevalier joined a [[Jewish Voice for Peace]] protest asking Senators [[Kirsten Gillibrand]] and [[Chuck Schumer]] to vote against [[United States support for Israel in the Gaza war#Military support|selling weapons to Israel]]. Police arrested protesters, including Avila Chevalier, whose shirt read "fund people, not bombs".<ref name= "ColumbiaSpectator2026Lee" /><ref>{{Cite news |last= McMenamin |first= Lex |date= April 15, 2026 |title='Fund people, not bombs': inside the US movement against war in Iran |url= https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/15/anti-war-protest-iran |access-date=June 1, 2026 |work= [[The Guardian]] |language= en-GB |issn= 0261-3077}}</ref><ref name= "JTA2026Strauss">{{Cite web| last= Strauss |first= Joseph |date= May 29, 2026 |title= Mamdani endorses former Columbia encampment organizer Darializa Avila Chevalier |url= https://www.jta.org/2026/05/29/ny/mamdani-endorses-former-columbia-encampment-organizer-darializa-avila-chevalier |access-date= June 1, 2026 |website= [[New York Jewish Week]] |language= en-US}}</ref> In March 2026, she participated in a Columbia University rally calling for the release of Khalil and [[Leqaa Kordia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Gao |first1= Dora |last2= Meerbaum |first2= Pedro |last3= Pillai |first3= Daksha |date= March 9, 2026 |title= Mahmoud Khalil, SIPA '24, addresses dozens at rally marking one year since ICE arrest |url= https://www.columbiaspectator.com/news/2026/03/09/mahmoud-khalil-sipa-24-addresses-dozens-at-rally-marking-one-year-since-ice-arrest/ |access-date= June 21, 2026 |website= Columbia Daily Spectator}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= Dias |first= Geovany |date= March 9, 2026 |title= Advocates rally for the release of a woman held by ICE for nearly a year |url= https://pix11.com/news/advocates-rally-for-the-release-of-a-woman-held-by-ice-for-nearly-a-year/ |access-date= June 21, 2026 |website= PIX11}}</ref> In September 2026, Avila Chevalier and more than 100 protesters were arrested at a protest of a speech by Israeli prime minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] at the [[Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly|United Nations General Assembly]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= Davis |first= Emma |date= September 25, 2026 |title= Hannah Einbinder & Susan Sarandon Arrested at UN Protest |url= https://www.thepinknews.com/2026/09/25/susan-sarandon-hannah-einbinder-caleb-hearon-un-protest-2026/ |access-date= September 25, 2026 |website= PinkNews |language= en-US}}</ref>

=== Foreign policy ===
==== Israel and Palestine ====
Avila Chevalier has been "unequivocal in condemning Israel as an [[Israeli apartheid|apartheid state]] committing [[Gaza genocide|genocide]]".<ref name="CityState2026Coltin">{{Cite web |last=Coltin |first=Jeff |date=June 4, 2026 |title=Avila Chevalier attended the Oct. 8 pro-Palestinian rally Lander condemned |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/avila-chevalier-attended-oct-8-pro-palestinian-rally-lander-condemned/413981/ |access-date=June 18, 2026 |website=[[City & State]] |language=en}}</ref> In March 2026, during a forum with the Broadway Democrats political club, Avila Chevalier, when asked whether she [[Do you condemn Hamas?|condemned Hamas]] for the [[October 7 attacks]], responded: "The premise of that question, to me, ignores the 75 years of occupation that the Palestinian people have been subjected to and the conditions that folks were living under before this genocide began."<ref name="CityState2026Coltin" /> When asked about condemning Hamas again in June, she said she did but added, "As far as I know, the US does not send a single dime to Hamas. What we fund is the Israeli military."<ref name="CityState2026Coltin" />

On October 8, 2023, Avila Chevalier attended a pro-Palestinian rally in [[Times Square]], a day after the [[October 7 attacks|October 7 Hamas attacks on Israel]]. The rally was organized by the [[Party for Socialism and Liberation]] and was criticized by numerous New York politicians—including [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]], [[Brad Lander]], and [[Kathy Hochul]]—as condoning the violence carried out by [[Hamas]] during the attacks.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite news |last= Pengelly |first= Martin |date= October 10, 2023 |title= AOC decries 'bigotry and callousness' of pro-Palestinian rally in New York |url= https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/oct/10/aoc-palestinian-rally-new-york |access-date= June 23, 2026 |work= [[The Guardian]] |language= en}}</ref><ref name="Website-2" /><ref name="CityState2026Coltin" /> In an interview with ''City & State'', Avila Chevalier said: "I can only say I have been advocating for the human rights of Palestinians for my adult life. And as someone who has seen a pattern, whenever anything happens on the ground [in Israel], there's always a really outsized reaction that costs thousands of people their lives."<ref name= "Website-2">{{Cite web |last=Coltin |first=Jeff |date=2026-06-04 |title= Avila Chevalier attended the Oct. 8 pro-Palestinian rally Lander condemned |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/avila-chevalier-attended-oct-8-pro-palestinian-rally-lander-condemned/413981/ |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref><ref name="CityState2026Coltin" />

Avila Chevalier has been active in protests against [[United States support for Israel in the Gaza war|US support for Israel]] and strongly criticized Espaillat's support of [[Israel]] and acceptance of campaign funds from [[AIPAC]] during the primary.<ref name="CityState2026Sterne" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Giardina |first= Isabella |date= June 5, 2026 |title= Community organizer launches primary challenge in NY-13 race |url= https://brooklyn.news12.com/2026/06/05/community-organizer-launches-primary-challenge-in-ny-13-race/6xmVJRGMyrTVg5t8zEf8bc |access-date= June 5, 2026 |website= News 12 |language= en}}</ref><ref name= "Crains2026">{{Cite web |last= Barkan |first= Ross |date=April 6, 2026 |title= On Politics: The next AOC-style upset might be brewing uptown |url= https://www.crainsnewyork.com/politics-policy/on-politics/cny-barkan-adriano-espaillat-primary-race-20260406/ |access-date= June 21, 2026 |website= Crain's New York Business}}</ref> In an interview with ''[[Jewish Currents]]'', she said Espaillat "has used his time in Congress to give ICE billions, fund the Israeli military, and vote for Trump's crypto corruption—while being bankrolled by AIPAC and the real estate lobby".<ref>{{Cite web |last= Kane |first= Alex |date= May 21, 2026 |title= Despite Anti-AIPAC Rhetoric, Congressional Progressives Rally Behind AIPAC-Backed Incumbent |url= https://jewishcurrents.org/despite-anti-aipac-rhetoric-congressional-progressives-rally-behind-aipac-backed-incumbent |access-date= June 1, 2026 |website= Jewish Currents |language=en}}</ref>

Avila Chevalier supports the [[Block the Bombs Act]], which would limit the sale, transfer, or exporting of defense articles and services to Israel.<ref name= "JTA2026Strauss" /> In June, [[American Priorities]], a [[super PAC]] established to oppose AIPAC, pledged funding to support Avila Chevalier, [[Claire Valdez]], and [[Brad Lander]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1= King |first1= Maya |last2= Fandos |first2= Nicholas |date= June 2, 2026 |title= Group Pledges $2 Million to Fight AIPAC in House Races |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/02/nyregion/aipac-spending-campaign-super-pac.html |access-date= June 5, 2026 |work= The New York Times |language= en-US |issn= 0362-4331}}</ref>

==== Iran War ====
In April 2026, as wars continued in [[Iran]], [[Lebanon]], and Palestine, Avila Chevalier participated in protests in [[Manhattan]] against the sending of weapons to Israel and was arrested during the protest. Chevalier said at the protest that the people of [[New York City|New York]] are tired of hearing that there is insufficient funding for childcare and healthcare services, while billions of dollars are being spent on killing.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McMenamin |first=Lex |date=2026-04-15 |title='Fund people, not bombs': inside the US movement against war in Iran |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/15/anti-war-protest-iran |access-date=2026-11-04 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> In August 2026, in response to a question about the [[2026 Iran war|Iran war]], she said that the costs of this war could have been spent on providing universal childcare services.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Newsource |first=C. N. N. |date=2026-08-24 |title=This democratic socialist has upset the party establishment. Here's her strategy for Congress |url=https://ktvz.com/politics/cnn-us-politics/2026/08/24/this-democratic-socialist-has-upset-the-party-establishment-heres-her-strategy-for-congress/ |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=KTVZ |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== Ukraine ====
In 2022, Avila Chevalier tweeted that the reason the United States was involved in the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]] was that "the Cold War ended and we've been bullying Russia ever since".<ref name= "NYTimes2026June14Goldenberg" /><ref>{{Cite tweet |user= darializabonet |number= 1496489018565009411 |title= Cause the Cold War ended and we've been bullying Russia ever since. Also war is lucrative for these sociopaths... |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220223142107/https://twitter.com/darializabonet/status/1496489018565009411|archive-date= February 23, 2022}}</ref> In a 2026 interview, she said she believed Ukraine was a victim of Russia's violation of its sovereignty, and that diplomacy with Russia should be pursued.<ref name= "NYEdBoard2026" />

=== Housing ===
Avila Chevalier supports universal housing, stronger tenant protections, and federal funding to build more [[social housing]].<ref name="CityState2026SterneSpar" /><ref name="Guardian2026Sainato" /> She has criticized [[gentrification]] and displacement in the district, saying that over 200,000 Black New Yorkers have left the city in the last 20 years.<ref name="Guardian2026Sainato" />

=== Healthcare and social spending ===
Avila Chevalier supports [[universal healthcare]] through [[Medicare For All]].<ref name="Guardian2026Sainato" /><ref name="Guardian2026Speri" /> "Babies Not Bombs" was a signature pledge of her campaign.<ref name="Guardian2026Speri" /><ref name="Guardian2026Sainato" /> She has called for federal resources to be directed toward schools, housing, and social safety-net programs.<ref name="Guardian2026Sainato" /><ref name= "Guardian2026Speri" />

=== Campaign finance and corporate power ===
Avila Chevalier supports banning large [[Political action committee#Super PACs|super PACs]] from elections and prohibiting members of Congress from trading stocks.<ref name="Guardian2026Sainato" />

=== Billionaires ===
In an interview with [[Ryan Grim]] on the podcast ''[[Breaking Points]]'', she agreed with [[Fran Lebowitz]]'s suggestion that billionaires threatening to leave New York City should do so.<ref name="BreakingPoints2026">{{Cite AV media |url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xRV2FCaZk5g |title=Fran Lebowitz Tells NYC Billionaires JUST LEAVE |date= May 22, 2026 |publisher= Breaking Points |access-date= June 11, 2026 |via= YouTube}}</ref>

=== Immigration ===
Avila Chevalier supports [[Abolish ICE|abolishing ICE]],<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Keith |first1=Tamara |last2= Gringlas |first2= Sam |last3= Lopez |first3= Ashley |last4= Moore |first4= Elena |date= February 6, 2026 |title= How fights over ICE funding are playing out on the Hill and in midterm races |url= https://www.npr.org/2026/02/06/nx-s1-5704204/how-fights-over-ice-funding-are-playing-out-on-the-hill-and-in-midterm-races |access-date=June 11, 2026 |website=NPR |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Moore |first= Elena |date=February 4, 2026 |title=Will Calls to 'Abolish ICE' Sway Voters in 2026? The Strategy Has Democrats Split |url= https://www.npr.org/2026/02/04/nx-s1-5690180/will-calls-to-abolish-ice-sway-voters-in-2026-the-strategy-has-democrats-split |access-date=June 11, 2026 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref> expanding [[Path to citizenship|pathways to citizenship]] for immigrants in the US,<ref name="ElDiario2026" /> and opposes all forms of [[deportation]], saying in a June 2026 interview, "I have yet to come up with a reason for why deportation has been used in a way that isn't rooted in deeply racist ideology." When [[Astead Herndon]] asked her about the deportation of people convicted of breaking [[Criminal law of the United States|US criminal law]], she responded that she opposed it, saying:<blockquote>We have a criminal system. It isn't perfect, but it exists, and if it is one that we accept as the process by which we want to engage with these issues—issues of harm, issues of criminality, or what have you—then we need to make sure that it isn't one that is also discriminatory on the basis of where people were born.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url= https://www.youtube.com/shorts/hIL98nnu3RY |title= Congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier believes all deportations are wrong |language=en |publisher=Vox |access-date=June 27, 2026 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref></blockquote>When asked about [[open border]]s, Avila Chevalier called free movement an "ideal vision", saying, "capital can move freely across the world, but people are trapped."<ref name="NYEdBoard2026">{{Cite web |date=June 18, 2026 |title=Darializa Avila Chevalier on Housing, Immigration, & Her Run for Congress in New York's 13th District |url= https://nyeditorialboard.substack.com/p/darializa-avila-chevalier-on-housing |access-date=June 24, 2026 |work=The New York Editorial Board |publisher=[[Substack]]}}</ref> In 2025, Avila Chevalier wrote an [[op-ed]] in ''[[USA Today]]'' calling for the freedom of [[Mahmoud Khalil]] after he was taken from his home and [[Detention of Mahmoud Khalil|detained by ICE]], writing:<blockquote>Immigration courts and detention centers have, for decades, been an abuse of administrative power. By targeting Mahmoud, Trump is now taking this abuse of power to a whole new level and making an example of him to silence those speaking out for the lives and human rights of Palestinians.<ref name= "USAToday2025Avila" /></blockquote>

=== Policing and public safety ===
Avila Chevalier supports [[prison abolition]].<ref name= "NYEdBoard2026" /> She has said she wants to help transform the United States into a society without murders by investing in programs for mental health services, healthcare, housing, and social systems. She acknowledged incarceration for murderers is "just the reality of what is going to happen", but said she was presenting "a vision for what we should have".<ref name= :0/>

Avila Chevalier praised Mamdani's effort to create the Department of Community Safety, and said crime reduction correlates with funding for social safety nets.<ref name= "NYEdBoard2026" />

====Criticisms of the NYPD====
In October 2026, Avila Chevalier called for the removal of [[Jessica Tisch]] as New York City [[police commissioner]], saying, "The NYPD's Strategic Response Group must be disbanded as quickly as possible, and Commissioner Tisch must step down." Her comments came in response to the shooting of a suspected [[Illegal immigration|illegal immigrant]] by an [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] officer in the city. Avila Chevalier participated in protests in the wake of the shooting and the NYPD deployed officers to manage the situation.<ref name="Website-1" />

During an incident between protesters and police, video footage showed Avila Chevalier falling to the ground after being pushed by a police officer.<ref name="Website-1" /><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/shorts/YBhzj2DmWjU |title=Dem nominee on being shoved to ground by NYPD during anti-ice protest |date=2026-10-09 |access-date=2026-10-14 |via=YouTube|type=Video|url-status=live|publisher=CNN}}</ref> She later claimed the NYPD "escalat[ed] violence" between officers and protesters, saying she "was shoved to the ground" and "witnessed unmarked law enforcement cars hitting protesters as NYPD officers pushed people out of its path". Avila Chevalier also alleged that Tisch "attempted to justify the shooting" and "spent more time protecting a militia that [had] just shot someone than protecting New Yorkers".<ref name= "Website-1">{{Cite web |last=Bullis |first=Hailey |date=2026-10-09 |title=New York House candidate calls for head of NYPD to step down after ICE shooting |url=https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/immigration/4760948/darializa-avila-chevalier-jessica-tisch-nypd-new-york-ice-shooting/ |access-date= 2026-10-14 |website=Washington Examiner |language=en-US}}</ref> 

=== Socialism ===
Avila Chevalier is a democratic socialist and member of the Democratic Socialists of America.<ref name= "wp-binday" /> She said she came to her ideology through organizing work, her undergraduate and graduate studies, and the [[Black radical tradition]]. She described democratic socialism as "workers and people in general having ownership and dignity over their lives and their work, and achieving that democratically".<ref>{{cite web |title= In Harlem, a Democratic Socialist Takes On the Dem Machine |url= https://jacobin.com/2026/01/avila-chevalier-harlem-bronx-socialism |website= Jacobin |access-date= 29 August 2026}}</ref> She denied being a communist, and said the question was a distraction. She posted tweets favorable to communist leaders and Marxism around 2020.<ref name= CNN>{{cite web |title= Deleted tweets on Darializa Avila Chevalier's account had favorable references to communist leaders and Marxism |url= https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/29/politics/darializa-avila-chevalier-communism-tweets |website= CNN |access-date= 29 August 2026}}</ref>

Also in 2020, she critiqued the lack of Marxist literature in public libraries, including by [[Vladimir Lenin]], and reposted a post criticizing "banned books" displays for not including the works of [[Joseph Stalin]]. In 2026, she said that was because she believed in freedom of speech and access to all kinds of thought, especially in the wake of [[Book censorship in the United States|book censorship]].<ref name= :0/><ref name= CNN/>

===Impeachment of Donald Trump===
During an interview with ''[[Politico]]'', Avila Chevalier was asked whether she would support [[Impeachment|impeaching]] President [[Donald Trump]] once she took office. She replied: "That is something that Trump himself seems to want, and so my question is: Is that actually going to be meaningful accountability for the Trump administration? We are going to have to think about what is actually going to hold their feet to the fire."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporter |first=Arthur DelaneySenior |last2=HuffPost |date=2026-10-18 |title= Incoming Democrats Avoid 'Impeach The Motherf**ker' Rhetoric |url= https://www.huffpost.com/entry/democrats-impeachment-darializa-avila-chevalier_n_6ad23be2e4b0a7bf79b1c6af |access-date= 2026-10-18 |website= HuffPost |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Avila Chevalier is [[Afro-Latin Americans|Afro-Latina]].<ref name= "AmsterdamNews2025Long" /><ref name= Time2024Mansoor /> In 2018, she converted to [[Islam]].<ref name= "HellGate2026Staff">{{Cite web |last= Edwards |first= Jessy |date= May 29, 2026 |title= Darializa Avila Chevalier Thinks She Can Overthrow the 'Dean of Dominican Elected Officials' |url= https://hellgatenyc.com/darializa-avila-chevalier-congress-espaillat-mamdani-endorsement/ |access-date= June 5, 2026 |website= Hell Gate |language= en}}</ref><ref name= "CityState2026Pretsky" /> Since 2023, she has been in a romantic relationship with [[Ramzi Kassem]], who in 2026 became the chief legal counsel in [[Zohran Mamdani]]'s [[Mayoralty of Zohran Mamdani|mayoral administration]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= Sterne |first= Peter |date= July 1, 2026 |title= Darializa Avila Chevalier is dating Mamdani's lawyer Ramzi Kassem |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/personality/2026/07/darializa-avila-chevalier-dating-mamdanis-lawyer-ramzi-kassem/414579/ |access-date= |website= [[City & State]] |language= en|quote= "Ramzi Kassem and I met outside an ICE detention facility, both working to free someone unjustly held," she said in a statement. "Over the years, as we collaborated on different projects, our professional acquaintance became a friendship, which grew into a romantic relationship. I'm deeply grateful for such a loving, supportive partner – he's been a refuge these past few years. Like most couples, we value our privacy, and ask that it be respected."}}</ref>
